brief: Citadel Securities' Frank Flight applies an options framework to Iran's strategic calculus in the ongoing conflict. Iran's position resembles being long a high-strike oil call expiring around the US midterms: its leverage has risen as the conflict persisted and oil moved higher, since polling shows gasoline prices are politically costly for the White House. This implies Tehran's leverage is worth more before the midterms than after. With oil near local highs but showing signs of upside exhaustion, and only weeks left to the midterms, Iran is approaching peak gamma, close to the strike and close to expiry, where small moves in oil produce large swings in Iran's leverage (high convexity), even as accelerating time decay shortens the window to convert disruption of the Strait of Hormuz into political pressure. The note argues the rational move, as with an option holder facing elevated time decay, may be to monetize this leverage now by reopening Hormuz in exchange for ending the war, converting temporary convexity into a more durable political outcome.
